Detect sleep spindles

Source: R/compute_spindles.R
compute_spindles.Rd

Detects sleep spindles in an EEG channel with the algorithm of yasa.spindles_detect() in YASA (Vallat & Walker, 2021; YASA 0.8.1), which follows Lacourse et al. (2019), and reproduces its output: the same events, at the same sample positions, with the same properties (see Details).

Usage

compute_spindles(
  psg,
  channel = NULL,
  stages = NULL,
  freq_spindle = c(12, 15),
  freq_broad = c(1, 30),
  duration_s = c(0.5, 2),
  min_distance_ms = 500,
  thresh_rel_pow = 0.2,
  thresh_corr = 0.65,
  thresh_rms = 1.5
)

Arguments

psg

An mrpheus_psg object from prepare_psg().

channel

Character. EEG channel label. If NULL (default), the first non-bad EEG channel is used.

stages

Integer vector or NULL. Epoch indices in which spindles may occur (for example the N1, N2 and N3 epochs). If NULL, all epochs are used. As in YASA, the RMS threshold is computed within these epochs and samples outside them cannot start a spindle, but an event can extend a little beyond them (the smoothing spreads over 0.1 s).

freq_spindle

Numeric vector of length 2. Spindle band (Hz), as YASA's freq_sp. Default c(12, 15).

freq_broad

Numeric vector of length 2. Broadband filter (Hz). Its transition bands are chosen as MNE does for filter_data(): 25 % of the cutoff, at least 2 Hz, and no more than the cutoff for the high-pass. Default c(1, 30).

duration_s

Numeric vector of length 2. Minimum and maximum duration of a spindle (s), exclusive. Default c(0.5, 2).

min_distance_ms

Numeric or NULL. Spindles separated by less than this (ms) are merged. Default 500. NULL or 0 switches merging off.

thresh_rel_pow

Numeric or NULL. Minimum relative sigma power. Default 0.20. NULL switches the criterion off.

thresh_corr

Numeric or NULL. Minimum moving correlation. Default 0.65. NULL switches the criterion off.

thresh_rms

Numeric or NULL. Number of trimmed standard deviations above the mean for the moving RMS. Default 1.5. NULL switches the criterion off. At least one criterion must be given.

Value

A tibble with one row per detected spindle:

epoch

Integer. Epoch of the first sample of the spindle.

start_s

Numeric. Onset (s) relative to the start of epoch.

end_s

Numeric. Offset (s) relative to the start of epoch; can exceed the epoch length when the spindle crosses an epoch boundary.

duration_s

Numeric. Duration (s).

peak_freq_hz

Numeric. Median instantaneous frequency (Hz) of the sigma-filtered signal within the spindle (YASA's Frequency).

rms_uv

Numeric. Root mean square (uV) of the detrended broadband signal within the spindle (YASA's RMS).

channel

Character.

peak_s

Numeric. Time of the most prominent peak (s from the start of the first epoch; YASA's Peak).

amplitude_uv

Numeric. Peak-to-peak amplitude of the detrended broadband signal (uV; YASA's Amplitude).

amp_filtered_uv

Numeric. Peak-to-peak amplitude of the sigma-filtered signal (uV; YASA's AmpFiltered).

abs_power

Numeric. Median log10 instantaneous power of the sigma signal (YASA's AbsPower).

rel_power

Numeric. Median relative sigma power (YASA's RelPower).

oscillations

Integer. Number of oscillations: peaks at least 60 ms apart.

symmetry

Numeric. Position of the most prominent peak within the spindle, from 0 to 1 (YASA's Symmetry).

Details

The channel is band-passed twice with FIR filters (Hamming window, zero phase, as mne.filter.filter_data()) applied to the continuous signal: a broadband filter (freq_broad, default 1-30 Hz) and a sigma filter (freq_spindle, default 12-15 Hz, transition bands of 1.5 Hz). Three criteria are evaluated at every sample: the relative power of the sigma band in the broadband signal (a short-time Fourier transform with 2 s windows every 0.2 s, linearly interpolated), the moving correlation between the sigma and the broadband signal (0.3 s windows) and the moving RMS of the sigma signal (0.3 s windows; the threshold is the mean plus thresh_rms trimmed standard deviations within the accepted epochs, at most 10 uV). The number of criteria met at each sample is smoothed over 0.1 s and a sample belongs to a spindle where at least all but one of the criteria are met. Events closer than min_distance_ms are merged, and those whose duration is within duration_s are kept.

Amplitudes must be in uV. As YASA, the channel is skipped (with a warning) when the standard deviation of its central 90 % of samples is outside 0.1-1000 uV, which usually means a wrong unit.

The result was compared with yasa.spindles_detect() on the Sleep-EDF night SC4001E0 (8.8 h at 100 Hz, and a 6.5 h version at 256 Hz) with a stage mask that cuts through events: the numbers of events are equal (73 and 78), the start and end times are identical, and every property agrees to about 1e-11. The test suite checks the same agreement against stored YASA output on a synthetic EEG with spindles at 100 and 256 Hz (tests/testthat/test-yasa-spindle-parity.R).

Not implemented: YASA's multi_only and remove_outliers options, and its spindle - slow oscillation coupling.

References

Lacourse, K., Delfrate, J., Beaudry, J., Peppard, P., & Warby, S. C. (2019). A sleep spindle detection algorithm that emulates human expert spindle scoring. Journal of Neuroscience Methods, 316, 3-11.

Vallat, R., & Walker, M. P. (2021). An open-source, high-performance tool for automated sleep staging. eLife, 10, e70092. doi:10.7554/eLife.70092
